issues.failure_explanation: With $\Phi_{\boldsymbol{X}_T}(\boldsymbol z)=\mathbb E[e^{\mathrm{i}\boldsymbol z'\boldsymbol X_T}]$ (as defined in the Notation), the formula $\Re\int\Phi(\boldsymbol y+\mathrm{i}\boldsymbol R)\hat P(\boldsymbol y+\mathrm{i}\boldsymbol R)d\boldsymbol y$ equals the option price only for the convention $\hat P(\boldsymbol z)=\int e^{-\mathrm{i}\boldsymbol z'\boldsymbol x}P(\boldsymbol x)d\boldsymbol x$ (e.g., for $X_T\equiv c$ the stated definitions yield $P(-c)$ instead of $P(c)$). The Notation instead defines $\hat P$ with $e^{+\mathrm{i}\boldsymbol z'\boldsymbol x}$, under which the proposition's formula is false. The paper's own Table of payoffs is written in the $e^{-\mathrm{i}\boldsymbol z'\boldsymbol x}$ convention (basket put $\prod\Gamma(-\mathrm{i} z_j)/\Gamma(2-\mathrm{i}\sum z_j)$ on $\{\Im z_j>0\}$; under the stated definition it would be $\prod\Gamma(\mathrm{i} z_j)/\Gamma(2+\mathrm{i}\sum z_j)$ on $\{\Im z_j<0\}$), and all experiments use positive damping $R_j$ for puts, matching the table and not the definition. Consequently Assumption 1's condition $e^{-\langle\boldsymbol R,\boldsymbol x\rangle}P\in L^1_{bc}$ has the wrong sign for the operative convention: for the basket put with $R_j>0$, $\int e^{-\boldsymbol R'\boldsymbol x}P(\boldsymbol x)d\boldsymbol x$ diverges, so the stated hypothesis fails for the paper's own payoffs (the correct condition is $e^{+\langle\boldsymbol R,\boldsymbol x\rangle}P\in L^1$); the bound $\|\hat P(\cdot+\mathrm{i}\boldsymbol R)\|_\infty\le\|e^{-\langle\boldsymbol R,\cdot\rangle}P\|_1$ used in the GBM section inherits the same error, and the claim that these payoffs 'adhere to' Assumption 1 fails as stated.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: From \eqref{eq:mnig_conditions}, a sufficient condition to eliminate the singularity at the boundary is to set $\boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}}$ such that the matrix $\delta^2 T^2 \boldsymbol{\Delta} - 2 \boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}}^{-1} \succeq 0$.

Consequently, we constructed the matrix $\boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}}$ by setting $\boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}} = \boldsymbol{P} \diag(\frac{2}{\lambda_1 \delta^2 T^2}, \ldots, \frac{2}{\lambda_d \delta^2 T^2} ) \boldsymbol{P}^{-1} = \frac{2}{ \delta^2 T^2 } \boldsymbol{\Delta}^{-1}$.

issues.failure_explanation: From the paper's own asymptotics (eq:lap_pdf_as_exp, with $v=\frac{2-d}{2}$), $\psi_{lap}(\boldsymbol y)\sim C\,(\boldsymbol y'\tilde\Sigma^{-1}\boldsymbol y)^{(1-d)/4}e^{-\sqrt{2\boldsymbol y'\tilde\Sigma^{-1}\boldsymbol y}}$, so $r^{NIG}(\boldsymbol y)\sim \text{const}\cdot|\boldsymbol y|^{(d-1)/2}\exp(\sqrt{2\boldsymbol y'\tilde\Sigma^{-1}\boldsymbol y}-\delta T\sqrt{\boldsymbol y'\Delta\boldsymbol y})$. The definition of $h^{NIG}_1$ (eq:T_NIG) silently drops the polynomial factor $(\boldsymbol y'\tilde\Sigma^{-1}\boldsymbol y)^{(d-1)/4}$ present in eq:lap_pdf_as_exp. At the critical choice $\tilde\Sigma=\frac{2}{\delta^2T^2}\Delta^{-1}$ the exponential factor is identically $1$, so $r^{NIG}\sim\text{const}\cdot|\boldsymbol y|^{(d-1)/2}\to+\infty$ for every $d\ge2$ (logarithmic growth in the distance to the boundary of $[0,1]^d$), not the claimed finite limit $\sqrt{\det\tilde\Sigma}$. Hence the stated sufficient condition $\delta^2T^2\Delta-2\tilde\Sigma^{-1}\succeq0$ fails at equality for $d\ge2$, and the recommended critical construction does not eliminate the boundary singularity; only strict definiteness with margin makes the exponential decay dominate the polynomial growth. The strict cases (i)/(iii) and the univariate analysis (where the prefactor is $|y|^0$) are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry the polynomial prefactor through the asymptotics, correct case (ii) (the limit is $+\infty$ for $d\ge2$), and strengthen the condition from $\succeq0$ to strict definiteness with margin (e.g., $\tilde\lambda_j\ge(1+\epsilon)\frac{2}{\lambda_j\delta^2T^2}$), so that the exponential decay dominates the polynomial growth.
issues.overall_effect: Case (ii) of the multivariate NIG trichotomy, the sufficiency claim for $\succeq0$, the NIG row of Table 3, and the recommended construction $\tilde\Sigma=\frac{2}{\delta^2T^2}\Delta^{-1}$ (deployed in the numerics, e.g., $\tilde\sigma_j=\frac{\sqrt2}{T\delta}$) are unreliable for $d\ge2$: at the recommended parameters the transformed integrand is unbounded (log-type growth), so the promised singularity-free integrand fails in the multivariate regime.
issues.title: Multivariate NIG critical case: dropped polynomial factor makes the claimed finite limit false for $d\ge2$
issues.why_classification: The correction is contained (track one asymptotic factor and tighten an inequality) and the method, rates, and experimental conclusions survive since the residual growth is only logarithmic; but the stated guarantee for the recommended critical parameter choice must be withdrawn and the condition strengthened, which is more than a routine local edit.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the multivariate NIG experiments perform the domain transformation 'as proposed in Section 3.2' (i.e., within the stated boundary-growth condition). But the stated parameters ($\Delta=I_d$, $\delta=0.2$, $T=1$, $\tilde\sigma_j=\frac{1}{T\delta}=5$, i.e., $\tilde\Sigma=25I_d$, reading $\tilde\sigma_j$ as the scale of $\tilde\Sigma$ exactly as in the 15D caption where $\tilde\sigma_j=\frac{\sqrt2}{T\delta}=\sqrt{2/(\delta^2T^2)}$) give $\delta^2T^2\Delta-2\tilde\Sigma^{-1}=0.04I_d-0.08I_d=-0.04I_d\prec0$: case (i) of the paper's own trichotomy, i.e., per the paper's analysis the transformed integrand diverges at the boundary (for the 6D call on min, whose payoff transform decays only polynomially, the full ratio still diverges). The univariate rule $\tilde\sigma_j=\frac{1}{\delta T}$ does not transfer to the multivariate Laplace proposal, whose marginal decay rate is $\sqrt2/\tilde\sigma_j$; the multivariate framework requires $\tilde\sigma_j\ge\frac{\sqrt2}{\delta T}$, as indeed used in the 15D NIG experiment. (Under the alternative reading of a product of univariate Laplaces, the joint characteristic function $\exp(-\delta T\sqrt{y'\Delta y})$ still decays more slowly than the product proposal off the coordinate axes, so the boundary-growth condition is likewise violated.)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either set the experimental scales to the multivariate rule ($\tilde\sigma_j\ge\frac{\sqrt2}{T\delta}$, as in the 15D figure) and re-run the affected experiments, or withdraw/qualify the compliance claim and analyze the boundary growth of the deployed mixture-based estimator.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the 3D/6D NIG numerical validations deploy the condition-compliant transformation 'as proposed in Section 3.2' is contradicted by the stated experimental parameters; the reported RQMC performance for these experiments is not covered by the paper's stated guarantee (it is rescued only by the mild boundary growth of the mixture-based realization, which the paper's theory does not establish).
issues.title: Multivariate NIG experiments use univariate-rule scales that violate the paper's own boundary-growth condition
issues.why_classification: Restoring consistency requires re-parameterizing and re-running the affected experiments or retracting the compliance claim and supplying a new growth analysis for the deployed estimator; no mere local edit suffices, yet the method and headline conclusions survive.
